summary: Empty day: no confirmable new, in-scope innovation signal published in the last 24 hours across the free §1a-§1d sources or the §1e Saturday watchlist. The strongest in-scope material reviewed was all out of the 24-hour window or already covered: City of Moreton Bay's Australian-first AI-powered ('movement-based') traffic-signal pilot at the Moreton Parade/Paper Avenue intersection in Petrie (announced early-to-mid July, hardware to be installed late 2026 — a genuine watch-grade item, but out of window today); Maddocks' 'Bridging the Gap: AI risk and governance in local government' report on the AI governance gap in Victorian councils (launched late July, and thematically covered by the QUT responsible-AI report already logged 12 August); Wollongong's world-first Canva 'Goals Platform' community-engagement pop-up (event ran 7-9 August, already noted 5 August); and the 2026 National Awards for Local Government (23 June) and NSW Local Government Week Awards (7 August). City of Casey's $900k Commonwealth-funded mobile CCTV-trailer trial is out of scope under §3b (community-safety/policing). AU industry verticals in waste and roads (Waste Management Review, Inside Waste, Roads & Infrastructure, Infrastructure Magazine) surfaced only evergreen FOGO-rollout and recycled-materials pieces, no fresh in-window council pilot. Overseas equal-weight outlets (Bloomberg Cities, Route Fifty, Cities Today, Apolitical, LGIU / LocalGov.co.uk, LGNZ) and the §1d tertiary/research institutes (ANZSOG, UTS/IPPG, UNSW City Futures, the UK/US/Canada centres) returned only evergreen thought-leadership and out-of-window awards/reports. The §1e watchlist newsrooms and the latest available business papers / Councillor Notices of Motion yielded no fresh in-window innovation motion or pilot (expected — councils meet ~monthly and agendas drop only days before). Paid titles (AFR/SMH/LGC/MJ) were held to headline + standfirst and not used.
